_comment: Bundle v2 conformance vectors (docs/bundle-format.md §16, aleutian.proof.bundle.v2), computed by scripts/bundle-vectors.py from the spec: each case is built with one stated defect and its expected result declared from that construction, as for bundle_v1_vectors.json, whose structure this file shares. Entries are chain format v4 (leaf hash and chain hash v4, format-spec §2.0), checkpoints are v7 anchors (format-spec §9.2-§9.5, ML-DSA-65 context aleutian.proof.anchor.v7), record signatures are over aleutian.proof.record.v2 (sink-format §9.1, context aleutian.proof.record.v2), all made with dilithium-py from the same fixed key seeds as the v1 file. Keys by name; the trust of a case names the keys a verifier is given. Compare the parsed result (§9), never its bytes. A case's `signatures` lists signatures whose validity is the point (checkpoint index or entry index in the bundle's first chain), as verified by a v2 verifier: v7 context for checkpoints, record.v2 envelope and context for records. `too-large` is not represented (§15 note 1; the v2 value limit is 17,000,000). The real_export case is a bundle exported by proof sink export from a real sink (scripts/bundlefixture/real_export_v2.json), its expected result derived from what was built. Readings of the spec this file pins: (1) §16 §7.6 step e's "entry end_seq's stored chain_hash" is the entry at index end_seq (= entry_count-1, as §7.5's coverage is by index), not an entry found by its global_seq (cases sequence, global_seq_2_63_minus_1_accepted); (2) entry_count and end_seq are compared as integers in steps c and d (ok_checkpoint_counts_compared_as_numbers); (3) §16 §4.4's "no |" for anchor_id, previous_anchor_id and subject is kept as written, although v7's anchor chain hash would not need it; (4) the leaf hash and envelope take each member's parsed JSON string value (ok_entry_type_escaped_in_json); (5) a v1-shaped entry and a v4 erased-shape entry in a v2 bundle are unreadable `structure` (missing or unknown members, §4.3), and a v6 checkpoint is checkpoint-malformed (step a).

cases.name: ok_both_trusts
cases.note: entries 0 and 1 of A are disclosed and open (opened); entry 2 is committed; B ends with a genuine erasure, so its two events are erased

cases.name: ok_record_trust_only
cases.note: without checkpoint trust, checkpoints are still checked structurally (steps a-e) and counted; the erasure is signed, not anchored (§7.9, R6)

cases.name: unauthenticated_no_trust
cases.note: hashes recompute, but nothing establishes provenance (U1)

cases.name: unauthenticated_empty_bundle
cases.note: an empty bundle proves nothing (§9.2)

cases.name: unauthenticated_unanchored_tail
cases.note: checkpoint trust only: the entry after the last checkpoint is not authenticated

cases.name: ok_tail_truncated_to_earlier_checkpoint
cases.note: a chain cut back to an earlier checkpoint verifies: undetectable from the bundle (§1)

cases.name: ok_two_checkpoints
cases.note: checkpoint 1's previous_anchor_id and previous_anchor_hash are checkpoint 0's anchor_id and chain_hash

cases.name: failed_changed_inner_entry_id_checkpoint_only
cases.note: v1 reads this swap as ok (bundle_v1_vectors.json ok_swapped_inner_entry_id_checkpoint_only); in v2 the leaf hash covers entry_id: chain-hash. The chain hash and the checkpoint still match the stored hashes, so nothing else objects

cases.name: failed_changed_inner_salt_checkpoint_only
cases.note: the leaf hash covers the salt

cases.name: failed_changed_entry_type_checkpoint_only
cases.note: the leaf hash covers entry_type: chain-hash. The new label is also judged by §7.4 (a sink.erasure without the erasure hash). Every change of label adds a §7.4 problem, so no entry_type change reads ok in v1 either; this one is relabelling an event as an erasure

cases.name: failed_changed_inner_entry_id_record_trust_only
cases.note: the same change under record trust: the record signature covers entry_id and leaf_hash

cases.name: failed_changed_inner_entry_id_resealed_checkpoint_only
cases.note: entry 1's id changed and its leaf and chain hash recomputed: it is consistent with itself, and the next entry's previous_hash no longer links to it

cases.name: failed_last_entry_salt_resealed_checkpoint_only
cases.note: the last entry's salt changed and its hashes recomputed: only the checkpoint, which binds the tip's chain hash, objects

cases.name: failed_last_entry_salt_resealed_record_trust_only
cases.note: no checkpoint: the record.v2 signature binds leaf_hash, so it binds the salt (sink-format §9.1); a record.v1 signature would still verify

cases.name: duplicate_chain
cases.note: every copy keyed by position (§8, §9.3)

cases.name: duplicate_chain_three_extra
cases.note: [A, B, A, B, A]: three extra copies, the first at 2

cases.name: invalid_chain_id
cases.note: no envelope can be built with an invalid chain id: bad-signature without verifying (§7.7)

cases.name: duplicate_entry_id
cases.note: entry 1 repeats entry 0's id, and its leaf hash, chain hash and record signature are all computed over the repeated id: only the duplicate rule objects

cases.name: duplicate_entry_id_repeat_malformed
cases.note: the repeat counts whether or not it is itself well-formed (§7.1 step 4)

cases.name: sequence
cases.note: the checkpoint still binds: step e takes the tip at index end_seq (= entry_count-1, §7.5), whose stored chain_hash is unchanged, not an entry found by its global_seq

cases.name: chain_hash
cases.note: the record envelope does not include chain_hash; the checkpoint binds the tip's stored hash

cases.name: chain_hash_wrong_leaf_hash
cases.note: the stored leaf_hash does not recompute, and the stored chain_hash does not recompute over it: chain-hash once for the entry (§16 §7.2). The record.v2 signature covers leaf_hash

cases.name: chain_hash_wrong_leaf_hash_chain_hash_consistent
cases.note: the chain hash recomputes over the stored leaf_hash, but the leaf hash does not recompute: a verifier must check the leaf hash, not only the chain hash

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_tip_hash
cases.note: the checkpoint binds the tip's STORED chain hash

cases.name: entry_type
cases.note: hashed and checkpointed as sink.other; no record envelope can be built for that type, so bad-signature without verifying (§7.7)

cases.name: entry_type_empty
cases.note: entry_type is any string for the shape check (§16 §4.3): the empty string is hashed with length 0 and judged by §7.4. (format-spec §2.0 refuses it in a chain; a bundle does not)

cases.name: entry_type_decomposed_unicode_hashed_as_given
cases.note: a non-ASCII label, hashed as its UTF-8 bytes as given: a verifier that normalises gets chain-hash as well

cases.name: erasure_invalid_label_without_hash
cases.note: an event labelled sink.erasure, hashed and signed as such by the writer: the label is covered, so only the erasure-hash rule objects

cases.name: erasure_invalid_relabelled
cases.note: an erasure record labelled sink.event, hashed and signed as such: found by its hash whatever the label, so the events before it stay erased (§7.3), and it is not a genuine erasure

cases.name: erasure_invalid_at_entry_0
cases.note: entry 0 can never be a genuine erasure (sink-format §2); its record signature is valid

cases.name: erasure_invalid_relabelled_checkpoint_only
cases.note: a genuine erasure relabelled after it was written: in v2 the leaf hash covers the label

cases.name: erased_event_disclosed
cases.note: the disclosure opens; it outlived the erasure

cases.name: modified_salt_given_as_nonce
cases.note: the entry's salt (also 64 hex) in place of its nonce: the salt is in the leaf hash, never in the commitment (format-spec §8)

cases.name: erasure_from_stored_global_seq
cases.note: the erasure hash is built from the predecessor's STORED global_seq (1), not its index (0)

cases.name: erasure_after_malformed_entry
cases.note: an entry whose predecessor is malformed cannot hold the erasure hash (§7.3): E = -1

cases.name: ok_two_erasures
cases.note: E is the LAST erasure; the earlier one is still genuine

cases.name: signed_erasure_without_checkpoint
cases.note: both trusts, no checkpoint: the erasure is signed (§7.9)

cases.name: disclosed_on_erasure
cases.note: a misplaced disclosed is field-shape and the entry's only outcome (§7.1.3): it still holds the erasure hash, so E = 2 and the events before it are erased, but it is not a genuine erasure

cases.name: disclosed_content_noncanonical_base64
cases.note: non-canonical base64 is a value shape: field-shape, and the event gets no outcome

cases.name: ok_disclosed_content_65536_bytes
cases.note: the largest disclosed content allowed

cases.name: global_seq_2_63_minus_1_accepted
cases.note: 2^63-1 is in shape (hashed, signed, checkpointed); only the sequence rule objects. The checkpoint's end_seq is "2": the tip is entry index 2 (§7.5)

cases.name: ok_timestamp_leap_day
cases.note: timestamps are never ordered (temporal authority)

cases.name: ok_entry_type_escaped_in_json
cases.note: the leaf hash and the record envelope take the parsed string value (sink.event), not its JSON spelling

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_v6_anchor
cases.note: a complete, validly signed v6 checkpoint (bundle v1's shape, range by entry id, empty context) over these entries: a v2 bundle holds v7 checkpoints only (§16 §4.1)

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_version_6
cases.note: v7's members with version 6, signed

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_entry_count_as_number
cases.note: v7's entry_count is a JSON string (§16 §4.4)

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_range_by_entry_id
cases.note: v1's range members in a v7 checkpoint

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_start_seq_not_0
cases.note: start_seq 1, end_seq 2, entry_count 2: consistent and signed (format-spec §9.3 allows it), but a bundle checkpoint starts at "0" (§16 §4.4)

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_entry_count_not_end_seq_plus_1
cases.note: entry_count 2, end_seq 2, signed

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_entry_count_0
cases.note: entry_count "0" (end_seq "0"): entry_count >= 1

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_entry_count_over_2_63
cases.note: end_seq 2^63-1 is in grammar, but entry_count = end_seq + 1 = 2^63 is not (format-spec §2.1)

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_seed_id_with_non_seed_hash
cases.note: the seed id goes with the seed hash and no other (format-spec §9.3), signed

cases.name: checkpoint_malformed_anchor_id_with_pipe
cases.note: §16 §4.4 keeps "no |" for anchor_id although v7's anchor chain hash does not hash it

cases.name: checkpoint_signature_out_of_alphabet_record_trust_only
cases.note: the signature's shape is judged in step a, without checkpoint trust too

cases.name: checkpoint_signature_short
cases.note: 3306 bytes, canonical base64

cases.name: checkpoint_case_variant_member
cases.note: member names are case-sensitive

cases.name: checkpoint_escaped_duplicate_member
cases.note: duplicates are compared after unescaping

cases.note: §3's number rule, on created_at_ms (entry_count is a string in v7)

cases.name: checkpoint_over_1_mib

cases.name: ok_checkpoint_exactly_1_mib

cases.name: ok_checkpoint_created_at_ms_2_53_minus_1
cases.note: the largest number allowed is accepted

cases.name: ok_checkpoint_member_order_and_whitespace

cases.name: checkpoint_sequence_first_not_seed
cases.note: neither the seed id nor the seed hash at k = 0: consistent with each other (step a), wrong for a first checkpoint (step c)

cases.name: checkpoint_overreach
cases.note: entry_count 4 over 3 entries

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_anchor_chain_hash
cases.note: a wrong anchor chain hash, validly signed

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_v6_anchor_chain_hash
cases.note: the anchor chain hash computed with the v6 preimage (aleutian.anchor.v2:, no length prefix), signed: v7 uses its own (format-spec §9.4)

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_subject_not_length_prefixed
cases.note: the v7 preimage without the subject's length prefix, signed

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_by_record_key
cases.note: the two trust dimensions are separate (§6)

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_with_empty_context
cases.note: the v7 canonical bytes signed with the EMPTY context (v6's): MUST fail, the context is aleutian.proof.anchor.v7 (format-spec §9.5)

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_with_record_context
cases.note: signed with aleutian.proof.record.v2

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_hashml_dsa
cases.note: HashML-DSA (SHA-512) with the v7 context MUST fail: proof uses pure ML-DSA

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_over_v6_canonical_bytes
cases.note: signed with the v7 context over v6-form bytes: the signed bytes are v7's canonical form

cases.name: checkpoint_signature_repeated_hint_index
cases.note: a valid signature re-encoded with a repeated hint index: FIPS 204 Algorithm 21 refuses it

cases.name: checkpoint_series_second_fails
cases.note: the last PASSING checkpoint decides coverage

cases.name: checkpoint_series_stops_after_failure
cases.note: checkpoint 1 is valid but never checked, and does not count

cases.name: checkpoint_sequence_previous_anchor_hash
cases.note: the right previous_anchor_id with a previous_anchor_hash that is not checkpoint 0's chain_hash (validly signed, its chain hash computed over that hash): step c

cases.name: checkpoint_sequence_second_names_seed
cases.note: checkpoint 1 names the seed id and seed hash, as a first checkpoint does

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_chain_hash_from_seed
cases.note: checkpoint 1 names checkpoint 0 correctly, but its anchor chain hash starts from the seed hash: step e hashes the previous_anchor_hash member

cases.name: ok_checkpoint_counts_compared_as_numbers
cases.note: entry_count "10" after "9" grows (as text it would not), and "10" <= 10 entries

cases.name: checkpoint_overreach_counts_compared_as_numbers

cases.name: record_malformed_signature_alphabet

cases.name: record_signed_by_checkpoint_key
cases.note: the two trust dimensions are separate (§6)

cases.name: record_signed_over_v1_envelope
cases.note: a valid record.v1 signature (v1 envelope, empty context) of this entry: a v2 bundle's record signatures are record.v2 (§16 §7.7)

cases.name: record_signed_with_empty_context
cases.note: the v2 envelope signed with the empty context MUST fail

cases.name: record_signature_repeated_hint_index
cases.note: a valid signature re-encoded with a repeated hint index: FIPS 204 Algorithm 21 refuses it

cases.name: record_signature_binds_salt
cases.note: entry 1's salt changed and its hashes recomputed, the original signature kept

cases.name: ok_malformed_record_signature_without_record_trust

cases.name: record_envelope_previous_hash_at_seq_0
